name: Split-Safety Invert Cover 2 Trap
coverage: Cover 2 Invert (Corners Deep Half, Safeties Underneath)

summary.motive: Deceive the quarterback by disguising a two-deep shell as single-high, inverting cornerbacks into deep halves while safeties trigger downhill to trap intermediate seams and out routes.
summary.keyDefender: FS (Downhill Invert Safety) & LCB (Deep-Half Sinking Corner)
summary.whyItWorks: Quarterbacks read the cornerback bailing deep and assume Cover 3, missing the safety driving downhill from 12 yards depth directly into the passing lane.
summary.failureMode: A deep post route between the sinking cornerbacks that exploits the vacant middle of the field if the safety triggers too aggressively downhill.

beats.title: Single-High Disguise Alignment
beats.text: Steve Spagnuolo shows a classic single-high Cover 1/3 look before the snap, encouraging the quarterback to work the weak slot out/seam route against presumed off coverage.

beats.title: The Invert Rotation
beats.text: At the snap, both cornerbacks bail aggressively to deep halves, while Free Safety (FS) screams downhill into the weak intermediate flat to spring the trap.

beats.title: The Trap Sprung (Interception)
beats.text: The QB throws to H expecting a soft Cover 3 flat void, but FS steps directly in front of the pass with downhill momentum for the interception.

beats.title: Pick-Six Return Underway
beats.text: With both outside cornerbacks already capping the deep boundaries, FS takes the turnover down the sideline for a game-changing score.

relations.tell: Corners sprint backwards into deep halves at snap while both safeties drive downhill into underneath curl/flat zones
